title: driver stacktrace bifurcation observations and nightshift mitigations
content:
Summary:

- Overnight (2029-01-14 01:12–04:03 UTC) we observed repeated kernel panics across three GPU nodes in cluster-gamma that initially looked like ECC-driven memory corruption. After triage, the evidence points to two diverging failure modes (bifurcation): one path dominated by correctable ECC spike + NVLink error messages, the other by an isolated GPU driver stacktrace referencing a specific nv-host driver symbol.

Why this doc exists: capture the bifurcation observations, commands we ran, immediate mitigations, and proposed runbook changes before we forget details in the morning handover. This is a working note — not final.

Hosts affected (examples taken from logs):
- gamma-node-07 (pinned to driver 540.84, GPUs: A100-40GB x8)
- gamma-node-12 (driver 545.29, GPUs: A100-80GB x4)
- gamma-node-19 (driver 545.29, GPUs: A100-80GB x8)

High-level timeline (UTC):
- 01:10 alert: automated ECC threshold alert fired (node gamma-node-07)
- 01:12 first kernel panic reported (gamma-node-07) — cluster-level evictions triggered
- 01:20 gamma-node-12 starts showing nvlink negotiation errors in dmesg
- 02:05 operator manually quarantined gamma-node-07 and disabled NVLink on the node (temporary kernel flag)
- 03:40 gamma-node-19 panicked with a stacktrace referencing nv-host module; ECC counters were low
- 04:03 cluster autoscaler drained remaining workloads from suspect hosts; incident escalated to platform oncall

What we saw in the logs (snippets):
- dmesg (gamma-node-12):
  [ 12543.432178] NVRM: NVIDIA GPU at PCI:0000:5e:00: Using NVLink lane 3 failed negotiation: status 0x34
  [ 12543.432181] nvidia: nvlink: link 3 failed to initialize, retrying
  [ 12543.465998] kernel: Correctable ECC error on GPU0: 32 counts (increasing)

- kernel oops (gamma-node-19) excerpt:
  "[ 21023.898765] nvidia 0000:65:00.0: panic in nv-host: rmmod?
   Call Trace:
     nvhost_event_handle+0x1a4/0x2b0 [nvhost]
     nvhost_batch_submit+0x3c8/0x6b0 [nvhost]
     nvidia_uvm_stack_dump+0x1d0/0x2c0 [nvidia]")

- note: stacktrace shows nvhost symbols rather than raw ECC corruption paths; ECC counters on this host were not elevated at time of panic (per telemetry snapshot).

Immediate triage actions taken (nightshift):
- Quarantined gamma-node-07 and gamma-node-19 from serving pool (k8s cordon + eviction) — operator: Diego Morales
- Rolled workloads to warm spare nodes; monitored latency regressions (none severe)
- For gamma-node-12 we disabled NVLink (module parameter: nvlink.link_enable=0 at boot) and rebooted to test stability; no further ECC spikes for 3h after reboot
- Collected full crash dumps and a copy of /var/log/nvidia-installer.log, /var/log/kern.log, and telemetry snapshots (ECC counters, GPU temps, NVLink error counters) and uploaded to incident artifact S3 path (linked in Jira)

Commands and snippets used (for handover / reproducibility):
- nvidia-smi -q -d ECC - shows ECC counts per GPU
- cat /proc/driver/nvidia/params | grep nvlink - show nvlink config bits
- dmesg --ctime | egrep -i "nvlink|ecc|NVRM|oops|panic" | tail -n 200
- sudo journalctl -k -u kubelet --since "2029-01-14 00:00" > /tmp/kubelet.log
- /usr/local/bin/collect-gpu-telemetry.sh gamma-node-07 --output /tmp/gamma-node-07-telemetry.tgz

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Configuration-path: NVLink negotiation flakiness (fabric layer) sometimes triggers heavy PCI/DMA activity that surfaces as correctable ECC counts; sustained retries push the driver into a pathological code path causing an nvhost-related panic (path bridging). Evidence: nodes with active NVLink retries had both ECC spikes and later driver oopses.
2) Driver regression: versions 545.x show a new nvhost scheduling path that can dereference stale pointers under specific timing with NVLink retransmits. Evidence: gamma-node-19 (545.29) panicked without ECC spikes.
3) Hardware aging: a subset of NVLink lanes on A100 cards show intermittent negotiation failures under thermal stress; may be exacerbated by PCIe retraining. Evidence: gamma-node-12 had persistent lane 3 failures and elevated PCB temps in telemetry.

Open questions / data to collect:
- Can we reproduce the panic deterministically? (short: no, it was intermittent overnight)
- Are there common batches/serials across affected GPUs? Need inventory to correlate serial numbers/firmware builds
- Are there earlier soft ECC patterns in the days prior (low-level increasing correctables) that predict panic?
- What exactly in driver 545.x changed vs 540.x relevant to nvhost scheduling? Attach diff/PR notes from driver release.

Short-term mitigations proposed (to implement before broader rollout):
- Add an automated NVLink-negotiation-alert that triggers at first retry spike (threshold: >5 retries/min for any link) and escalates to SRE before ECC thresholds are hit
- For nodes where nvlink negotiation repeatedly fails, automatically disable NVLink (module param) and mark node for hardware inspection in next maintenance window
- Pin cluster-gamma to driver 540.84 temporarily for nodes that reproduced the panic (rollback plan in PR #88)
- Expand telemetry sampling to include per-link retry ticks at 10s cadence for 72h on suspect nodes

Longer-term actions / runbook proposals:
- Runbook addition: a new NVLINK_TROUBLESHOOTING section that prescribes:
  1) Immediate cordon + collect telemetry + copy dmesg/journal
  2) Check /proc/driver/nvidia/params and ECC counters
  3) If nvlink retry rate > threshold -> disable NVLink, reboot, validate stability for 4h -> if stable, schedule hardware bench test; if not stable, retire card
  4) If stacktrace references nvhost -> take kernel oops dump with krashed tools and collect kdump, escalate to platform/driver team with full vmcore
- Create a small lab script to fuzz NVLink negotiation (synthetic lane flapping) to see if we can trigger the nvhost panic locally in the lab environment
- Track downstream driver vendor fixes and prepare staged rollout test across one pool before cluster-wide upgrade

Action items (owners and ETA):
- Diego: upload full vmcore and crash artifacts to S3 + attach to SRE-4127 (ETA: 2029-01-15 09:00)
- Priya: correlate hardware serials for affected GPUs and request vendor trace tooling if pattern holds (ETA: 2029-01-18)
- Samir: implement NVLink retry alert in observability (Grafana/alertmanager rule + slack playbook) (ETA: 2029-01-17)
- Ava (me): draft runbook NVLINK_TROUBLESHOOTING and PR to sops-runbooks repo (ETA: 2029-01-20)

Notes to self (informal):
- Night was messy. We got lucky with spare capacity. If cluster under higher load this would have been customer-visible.
- Keep the panic stacktrace — it looks like a use-after-free in nvhost_event handling; vendor driver folks need both nvhost.log and vmcore.
- Double-check that the disable-NVLink measure doesn't mask other failure signals (we still capture kernel oops after module param change?).

References / links:
- Incident ticket: SRE-4127 (linked_artifacts above)
- Slack thread: #gpu-oncall (https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0GPUONCALL/p1670000000000000)
- Driver rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/driver-fixes/pull/88

Appendix: quick sample kdump retrieval command for handover
- mkdir -p /tmp/incident-dumps && scp root@gamma-node-19:/var/crash/vmcore-$(date +%s) /tmp/incident-dumps/
- tar czf /tmp/incident-dumps/gamma-node-19-20290114.tgz /tmp/incident-dumps/*

End of notes — please add observations and corrections.
